Wednesday, November 18, 2026

Space & Defense Daily — Wednesday, Nov 18, 2026

EU proposes a €45B 2027 loan for Ukraine and Kubilius urges capitals to swap Patriot stocks to Kyiv now; Senate appropriators move to bar >$100M sole-source Space Force awards for SDN and SB-AMTI after $6.45B to SpaceX as Golden Dome's C2 enters testing; ICEYE's €2B+ bid for Avio draws a cool response from Rome.

← NewerLatestAll briefingsOlder →Tue, Nov 17, 2026
NATOEuropean UnionUnited StatesEuropean spaceGlobal space & defense

Top stories: The European Commission proposed a €45B loan for Ukraine in 2027, with €25B for weapons. Defence Commissioner Kubilius also urged EU capitals to hand Kyiv Patriot interceptors from their own stocks now and take Ukraine's 2028–29 deliveries in exchange. In Washington, Senate appropriators want to bar sole-source Space Force awards over $100M for the Space Data Network and SB-AMTI after SpaceX won $6.45B in those programs. Golden Dome officials say its command-and-control layer is now in testing, but funding uncertainty is growing. In European space, ICEYE launched a €2B+ cash bid for Avio, Italy's Vega rocket maker, and Rome's first response was cool.

NATO

  • NATO published a summary of its first Alliance-wide Next Generation Communication Networks Strategy, which covers 5G, 6G and SATCOM. It stresses resilience against untrusted vendors and cyber threats, and an implementation roadmap is in work, with a Finnish–Swedish innovation range for testing. (NATO)
  • Wrapping up Tuesday's Ukraine Defence Contact Group, Rutte welcomed "hundreds of millions" in new PURL pledges and said Ukraine needs support "not only this winter, but also beyond." He goes to Berlin Thursday (Nov. 19) for the Coalition of the Willing meeting hosted by Merz, Macron and Burnham. (NATO; NATO)
  • Rzeczpospolita reports that Russian intelligence planned a mass-casualty false-flag attack near Poland's border with Kaliningrad in late October or early November, to be blamed on Ukraine. Warsaw quietly reinforced the border with police counter-terror units and GROM/AGAT exercises, and the Baltic states were also warned. (Kyiv Independent)

European Union

  • The Commission proposed a €45B loan for Ukraine in 2027: €25B for weapons and €20B for civilian needs. Kyiv would repay it only once Russia pays reparations. Slovakia, Czechia, Hungary and Bulgaria say they won't take part, and Merz threatens to block the next EU budget unless everyone joins. (The Guardian)
  • Kubilius urged member states to swap Patriot missiles from their stocks to Ukraine now and take Kyiv's already-ordered 2028–29 deliveries in return. He estimates Russia will fire about 2,000 ballistic missiles at Ukraine this year, versus US output of about 700 interceptors a year. (Rapporteur)
  • At the European Business Summit, Kubilius said Russia's €180B military budget for 2027 matches all EU states combined in purchasing-power terms, and that some European air-defence suppliers can't deliver to Ukraine until 2028–29. He cited the five new EDPCIs (drones, space, maritime), IRIS² service from 2029 and Galileo PRS from 2027, and named launch capacity as Europe's biggest space gap. (EU Perspectives)
  • Draft conclusions for Friday's EU–UK summit point to closer defence-industrial cooperation, including via the "Capability Coalitions." France is still pushing to limit British firms' access to SAFE. (Euronews)

United States

  • Senate appropriators' FY27 bill would bar the Space Force from sole-source or noncompetitive awards above $100M for the Space Data Network and SB-AMTI, after SpaceX won $6.45B across the two this year. It sets the Space Force topline at about $54.7B, below the House's $55.5B and the $59.2B request. (SatNews; SpaceNews)
  • Golden Dome: deputy director Marcia Holmes says the C2 layer finished a multi-domain virtual tracking exercise. It is now in a testing campaign heading toward integrated demos in 2027 and IOC in 2028. (Aerospace America)
  • An L3Harris executive said Golden Dome's future depends on moving to regular annual appropriations, as uncertainty over its financing grows after the midterms. (SpaceNews)
  • A new GAO report says the shift to proliferated LEO constellations (about $33B over five years) is straining the space industrial base. Chip and circuit-board shortages have delayed PWSA and MEO missile-warning launches, and GAO wants enterprise-wide supply-chain oversight across the Department of the Air Force and NRO. (DefenseScoop)
  • The Space Force's Commercial SATCOM Office awarded Eutelsat Network Solutions (OneWeb) a two-year Warrior Plans contract worth over $60M. It covers LEO airtime, deployable terminals and alternative PNT for tactical users. (Military Aerospace)
  • SNC and Specter Aerospace won a $124M Air Force contract for a ground-launched supersonic counter-air missile under the new Counter-Air Missile Program (CAMP). (Aviation Week)
  • The Pentagon failed its ninth straight financial audit ($4.9T in assets, $5.2T in liabilities). The comptroller is betting a new strategy can produce a clean opinion by 2028. (Breaking Defense)
  • NDAA: House Republicans are threatening to strip the bill's Ukraine provisions to force Democrats to drop language strengthening congressional oversight of Hegseth and Trump. (NBC News)
  • The White House formally nominated Gen. Christopher LaNeve as Army Chief of Staff, months after Hegseth ousted Gen. Randy George, with Lt. Gen. Marcus Evans as vice chief. Confirmation may need to happen before the new Congress in January. (Breaking Defense)
  • SpaceX is targeting Thursday, Nov. 19 at 8:28 p.m. PT for the classified USSF-317 Falcon 9 mission from Vandenberg. With Vulcan and New Glenn grounded, Falcon remains the only NSSL ride flying. (SpaceX)

European space

  • ICEYE has bid more than €2B for Avio to create an integrated European space-and-defence group. Italy's defence minister Crosetto told Leonardo, which owns 18%, to "think carefully" before selling. The deal needs golden-power clearance, and Avio trades just below the €41 offer. (CNA / Reuters; SpaceNews)
  • At Space Tech Expo Bremen, OHB signed a €102M ESA contract as prime for ClearSpace-1, Europe's first active debris-removal mission. It will capture the defunct PROBA-1 satellite and de-orbit it, with launch planned for 2030. (OHB)
  • Arianespace set the VA271 launch window: Ariane 64 with 36 Amazon Leo satellites on Nov. 23, 11:09–11:38 UTC (3:09–3:38 a.m. PT), from Kourou. It's Ariane 6's 10th flight. (Arianespace)
  • Mitsubishi Electric booked the second test flight of PLD Space's Miura 5 (debut targeted for H1 2027) to carry a demonstrator for its proposed megaconstellation. (SpaceNews)

Global space & defense

  • Iran widened its Gulf attacks, sending drones at Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait (the first attack there in two months) and launching more strikes on Bahrain. This followed US strikes on an IRGC missile site on Qeshm Island, and an ADNOC tanker crew member is missing after an attack in Hormuz. (BBC)
  • Russia launched 141 drones at Ukraine overnight (126 intercepted), hitting energy sites in Kyiv, Mykolaiv and Rivne oblasts. Five people were killed nationwide. (Kyiv Independent)
  • Trump arrived in Shenzhen and joined Xi and Putin at the APEC welcome banquet. Thursday brings a Trump–Xi bilateral and the first trilateral with Putin, after Putin used his APEC speech to claim Europe is losing ground. (CNBC)
  • China rolled Shenzhou-24 out to the pad at Jiuquan for launch "in the near future." It will be China's first crewed flight with a foreign astronaut, a Pakistani payload specialist. (CGTN)
